newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU commissioners likely to clear Ciba gene maize.
newsitem.headline: EU commissioners likely to clear Ciba gene maize.

text.p: European commissioners are likely to approve later on Wednesday market release of Ciba Geigy Ag's gene-altered maize, following expert advice but defying consumer and environment groups' opposition.
The approval, if confirmed, will follow the advice of three sets of EU scientists whose reports concluded there were no reasons to reject the maize, officials said.
European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has said the European Union must follow scientific advice on Ciba Geigy's gene-modified maize.
"There's not much alternative than to follow the scientific advice," he told Reuters following a two-day meeting of EU farm ministers ending on Tuesday. The ministers did not discuss gene-maize.

Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard, supported by the Health and Consumer Affairs commissioners, is likely to insist on monitoring maize shipments and some form of special labelling, Commission officials said.

Approval would ease the risk of increased trade tension between the 15-country EU and the United States, whose farmers have faced difficulties exporting to the bloc after growing their first crops containing the U.S.-cleared, gene-modified maize in this year's harvest.

But European consumers and environmental groups are likely to be less happy, having urged rejection or at least delays to approval on the grounds of uncertainty about the gene-altered maize's possible environmental effects.

The maize (corn) was developed by the Swiss chemical company to resist the herbicide glufosinate, commonly marketed as Basta, and to carry the Bt-toxin against corn-borer pests. The maize also carries an antibiotic "marker gene".

The European Consumers' Organisation (BEUC) added its voice to those of environmental campaigners last Friday when it urged the Commission to throw out the approval application, citing various fears about the effects of the release.
